description: This test ensures that users can successfully log in using the Google authentication option and are redirected to the dashboard upon successful login.
steps: Navigate to the login page at https://dev.roost.ai/login.
Verify that the Google authentication button is visible and enabled.
Click on the Google authentication button.
Wait for the Google login page to load.
Enter valid Google account credentials and submit the form.
Wait for the redirection back to https://dev.roost.ai.
Verify that the user is redirected to the dashboard.
Confirm that the user's name or email is displayed on the dashboard header, indicating a successful login.
expected_results: The Google login page is displayed when the Google authentication option is clicked.
The user is redirected to the dashboard after entering valid credentials.
The user's name or email is displayed on the dashboard, indicating a successful login.
edge_cases: The Google authentication button is not visible or enabled.
Invalid credentials are entered on the Google login page.
The redirection back to https://dev.roost.ai fails.
The Google authentication service is down.
The user closes the browser before completing the login process.
data_requirements: Access to the Google authentication service.
Pre-configured client ID and redirect URI for the application.
A valid session token for the user upon successful login.
dependencies: Google authentication service must be operational.
The application must have a valid client ID registered with Google.
The redirection URI must be correctly configured in the application's settings.
api_interactions: Roost backend API for session validation
performance_metrics: Time taken to load the Google login page.
Time taken to redirect back to the dashboard after successful login.
Time to display user-specific data on the dashboard.
accessibility_requirements: The Google login button should be accessible via a screen reader.
Keyboard navigation should allow users to focus on the Google login button.
The redirection process should not rely on time-sensitive actions that could hinder accessibility.
